title: Interrupting Interruption and the Art of Refusal
coreMove: Protect attention by publishing access rules: batch email, require meeting decisions, give permissions, and keep a true emergency path open.

exampleSpecs.audience: a team lead resetting response expectations
exampleSpecs.stakes: Constant replies are taking time from a release fix.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the email autoresponder to shift scheduled checking and urgent phone use into the social contract.

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations manager removing approval drag
exampleSpecs.stakes: Small refunds are freezing because every choice waits for the owner.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show missing permissions becoming decision rules and spending limits.

exampleSpecs.audience: an account director calming a nervous client
exampleSpecs.stakes: A client may read slower email as neglect unless the rule is explicit.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use scheduled checking plus urgent phone language to make refusal respectful.

exampleSpecs.audience: a floor supervisor reducing routine approvals
exampleSpecs.stakes: The line keeps stopping for small purchases the crew could handle.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a bottleneck caused by missing spending limits, then repair it.

exampleSpecs.audience: a product lead deciding whether to accept a vague invite
exampleSpecs.stakes: A no-agenda meeting may consume the one block needed for planning.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Translate batching and scheduled checking into a refusal script for meetings.

exampleSpecs.audience: a desk lead keeping cases moving
exampleSpecs.stakes: Case files are pausing because staff fear making small calls alone.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Expose missing permissions as the cause of repeated interruptions.
